newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chirac fails bolster popularity with TV pleas - poll.
newsitem.headline: Chirac fails bolster popularity with TV pleas - poll.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac's appeals for understanding of his austerity policies have failed to lift his low popularity, an opinion poll indicated on Thursday.

The CSA survey, for the daily Le Parisien, showed that 51 percent of those polled had a bad opinion of conservative Chirac, up from 48 percent in a comparable survey in September. Those with a good opinion were unchanged at 43 percent.

The survey was taken among 1,001 people on December 13, the day after Chirac gave a marathon television interview in which he reaffirmed that the government's austerity policies were the best cure for record unemployment of 12.6 percent.
He also ruled out a cabinet reshuffle in the interview, his first extended questioning since July.
A poll on Tuesday had shown a slight rise in Chirac's popularity even though French people said his television was performance unconvincing.

Prime Minister Alain Juppe fared even worse in the Le Parisien poll. The percentage of those with a bad opinion of Juppe rose four points to 60 percent and those with a good opinion fell three points to 31.

The main comfort for Chirac and Juppe was that opposition Socialist leader Lionel Jospin failed to cash in on their unpopularity. People with a good opinion of Jospin fell one point to 46 percent while those with a bad opinion were unchanged at 44 percent.
